---
title: "Installing & Building RISC-V Toolchain"
date: "2021-05-21"
categories: [RISC-V]
description: "A walkthrough of installing and building the RISC-V toolchain from scratch on Ubuntu 20 LTS."
---

This post walks you through how to install and build the [RISC-V toolchain](https://github.com/riscv/riscv-gnu-toolchain) from scratch.

## Prerequisites

- Install `git` on your system:

```bash
sudo apt install git-all
```

- A Linux machine (tested on Ubuntu 20 LTS).
- Sufficient storage — around 30 GB free.
- Install a few dependencies:

```bash
sudo apt-get install autoconf automake autotools-dev curl python3 \
  libmpc-dev libmpfr-dev libgmp-dev gawk build-essential bison \
  flex texinfo gperf libtool patchutils bc zlib1g-dev libexpat-dev
```

## Create a directory and clone

```bash
mkdir risc-v
cd risc-v
git clone https://github.com/riscv/riscv-gnu-toolchain
```

## Create a directory in `/opt`

```bash
mkdir /opt/riscv
```

## Configure and make

```bash
./configure --prefix=/opt/riscv
make linux
```

This might take several hours depending on your machine configuration. The tool will be available in `/opt/riscv/bin`.

## Add `/opt/riscv/bin` to `PATH`

Open `~/.bashrc`:

```bash
sudo gedit ~/.bashrc
```

Add near the end of the file and save:

```bash
export PATH="$PATH:/opt/riscv/bin"
```

Now the RISC-V tools will be available without specifying the path.
